interpretation: The historical v1.1 checkpoint likely predates GSE244832, GSE296875, and GSE289173, so chronology supports target-label-unexposed status if its declared MD5 verifies. That does not make it admissible. The repository has no code license, no separate checkpoint terms were detected, the archive lacks a frozen SHA-256/size/inventory, loading is unsafe until inspected, the runtime is a legacy 2020 stack, and the checkpoint was trained on blood and colorectal cells rather than liver. The upstream local-training path also normalizes and clusters before splitting, which is leakage-incompatible.
remaining_blockers: Obtain written permission covering code execution, modification, trained derivatives, and any redistribution; obtain separate checkpoint use and derivative-weight terms.

Only after permission, acquire the archive under a controlled receipt and verify the declared MD5 plus SHA-256, byte size, immutable source identity, and a path-traversal-safe file inventory before extraction.

Resolve the checkpoint genome build and validate all 34,861 gene and 223,897 peak identifiers against GENCODE v49 and GRCh38.p14 with exact feature coverage/order.

Validate the Python 3.7/PyTorch 1.3 legacy model on an isolated L40S-compatible environment or document a numerically equivalent permitted port with fixed fixtures.
Prove RNA-only held-donor inference emits ATAC probabilities without target ATAC, updating, feature refitting, or calibration; compare calibration and liver domain shift explicitly.
